payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-05
payload.summary:
**ChatGPT** rolled out web-app publishing and a memory upgrade; **Codex** got a Python SDK while OpenAI disclosed a token undercount bug; **Anthropic** dominated the builder chatter with Claude writing most of its own code, a blunt Claude Code postmortem, and Managed Agents pushing deeper into enterprise infra; real-world evals, agent-native writing tools, and personal workflow automation kept the pressure on. 

**ChatGPT** 今天连发两下：能直接做并发布网页应用，记忆也升级了；**Codex** 一边放出 Python SDK，一边公开说修了计费少算 token 的 bug；**Anthropic** 这波声量最大，既有 Claude Code 事故复盘，也有 Managed Agents 往企业内网继续钻，还顺手放出一组很猛的内部数据，说 Claude 已经写了大部分自家代码；另一边，真实世界评测、给代理用的写作工具、个人工作流自动化，也都开始从概念往实战挪。

sections.headline: **OpenAI**’s Dan Roberts on RL, math breakthroughs, and AI discovery / **OpenAI** 的 Dan Roberts 谈强化学习、数学突破与 AI 发现
sections.body:
**Matt Turck** talks with **OpenAI** researcher **Dan Roberts** about why reinforcement learning has become central to modern frontier models, and why test-time reasoning is starting to matter for real scientific work. The discussion ties a volatile week in AI math to a broader shift: models are getting better not just at solving framed tasks, but at pursuing contrarian lines of thought long enough to uncover something new.

They also draw a sharp contrast between **OpenAI**’s more open-ended exploratory approach and **DeepMind**’s formal proof workflow in **Lean**. Roberts argues the path to AI-assisted science will likely be gradual, but the combination of language, RL, and sustained reasoning is already pushing models into territory that looks much closer to genuine research behavior.

**Matt Turck** 找来 **OpenAI** 的研究员 **Dan Roberts**，聊为什么强化学习已经成了前沿模型的核心，也聊测试时推理为什么开始真的影响科学研究。这期的背景是 AI 数学圈刚过了一周大新闻，重点不只是模型会做题，而是它们开始能沿着不那么顺手、甚至有点逆向的思路一直追下去，最后真挖出点新东西。

他们也把 **OpenAI** 和 **DeepMind** 的路线差别讲得很清楚：前者更像开放式探索，后者更强调在 **Lean** 里做形式化证明。Roberts 的判断不算夸张，意思也很明确: AI 变成科学助手不会是一夜之间的事，但语言能力、强化学习和长程推理叠在一起，已经把模型推到更接近“真研究”的地带了。

sections.headline: **Anthropic** details three separate **Claude Code** quality regressions / **Anthropic** 拆开讲清 **Claude Code** 的三次质量回退
sections.body:
**Anthropic** says reports of worsening **Claude Code** quality traced back to three product-layer changes rather than model or API degradation. The first was a March switch from high to medium default reasoning effort to cut latency; users felt the drop in intelligence quickly, and Anthropic reversed it. The second was a prompt-caching bug that kept clearing prior reasoning after an idle session, making Claude seem forgetful, repetitive, and oddly inconsistent. The third was a prompt tweak meant to reduce verbosity that ended up hurting coding quality and was rolled back.

The post is unusually direct about how hard the issue was to reproduce and why internal evals missed it. Anthropic says the incidents have been fixed, subscriber usage limits are being reset, and the company is expanding review context and guardrails so similar regressions are less likely to slip through again.

**Anthropic** 的说法很明确：大家感觉 **Claude Code** 变笨，不是底层模型坏了，也不是 API 出问题，而是产品层连续三处改动叠出来的。第一刀是 3 月把默认推理强度从 high 调到 medium，为了压延迟，结果用户很快就觉得智力掉了，于是又改回去。第二刀更伤，是缓存优化里的 bug，让空闲会话之后的历史推理被一轮轮清掉，Claude 就开始健忘、重复、工具乱用。第三刀是想压 verbosity 的系统提示词，结果把写代码质量也带崩了，最后撤回。

这篇复盘难得不打官腔，直接承认问题一开始很难复现，内部评测也没及时抓到。现在这几处都已经修掉，订阅用户的额度会重置，后面还会补更多审查上下文和防线，免得这种回退再悄悄溜过去。

sections.headline: **Managed Agents** splits the agent brain, hands, and memory / **Managed Agents** 把代理的大脑、手脚和记忆拆开了
sections.body:
**Anthropic** frames **Managed Agents** as an infrastructure redesign for long-running agents. The core move is architectural: separate the harness that calls Claude, the sandbox that executes tools and code, and the durable session log that stores what happened. That decoupling makes failures easier to recover from, lets sandboxes be replaced without losing the agent session, and avoids tying the entire system to one fragile container.

The post also shows the security and context-management logic behind the design. Credentials are kept out of the sandbox through repo-scoped auth and MCP proxies, while the session log becomes an external memory object the agent can revisit instead of relying only on the model context window. It reads like Anthropic trying to turn agent orchestration into a stable systems interface rather than a one-off harness hack.

**Anthropic** 这篇讲的不是功能小修小补，而是长程代理底座怎么重搭。核心动作很系统：把调用 Claude 的 harness、执行代码和工具的 sandbox、还有记录全过程的 session log 拆开。这样一来，哪块挂了就修哪块，sandbox 死了也不用把整场会话一起陪葬，整个系统不再绑在那种一坏就得人工抢救的单容器设计上。

它顺手也把安全和上下文管理讲透了。凭证不进 sandbox，Git 和 MCP 调用都走更窄的边界；长任务的记忆也不再死扛模型上下文窗口，而是放进可回读的 session log。读下来很像 **Anthropic** 在把 agent orchestration 从“工程师临时拼的 harness”往稳定接口层推。

sections.headline: **Claude Managed Agents** adds self-hosted sandboxes and private **MCP** tunnels / **Claude Managed Agents** 新增自托管沙箱和私有 **MCP** 隧道
sections.body:
**Claude Managed Agents** can now run tool execution inside customer-controlled sandboxes and connect to private **MCP** servers without exposing them to the public internet. Anthropic keeps the orchestration loop, but compute, files, packages, and internal services can stay inside the customer perimeter or inside managed providers such as **Cloudflare**, **Daytona**, **Modal**, and **Vercel**.

The update is aimed squarely at enterprise deployment friction: more control over runtime images and resource sizing, tighter auditability, and a cleaner path to internal databases, APIs, and knowledge systems. Self-hosted sandboxes are in public beta, while MCP tunnels are still in research preview.

**Claude Managed Agents** 现在可以把工具执行放进客户自己控制的 sandbox 里，也能连到私有 **MCP** 服务，而且不用把这些服务直接暴露到公网。Anthropic 继续托管编排循环，但算力、文件、依赖包和内部服务可以留在客户边界内，或者放在 **Cloudflare**、**Daytona**、**Modal**、**Vercel** 这些托管环境里。

这次更新瞄得很准，就是企业落地时最烦的那几件事：运行环境谁说了算，审计怎么做，资源怎么配，内网数据库和 API 怎么接。自托管沙箱已经公测，MCP 隧道还在研究预览阶段。

sections.headline: **Claude** expands connectors from work apps into everyday consumer services / **Claude** 把连接器从办公软件一路扩到日常消费应用
sections.body:
**Claude** is adding a new wave of consumer-facing connectors, including **AllTrails**, **Instacart**, **Audible**, **Tripadvisor**, **TurboTax**, **Uber**, and more. Anthropic says connectors can now surface dynamically inside conversation based on user context, so Claude can suggest the right app for tasks like finding reservations, groceries, or travel options instead of forcing people to browse a static tool list.

The pitch is convenience without ads or hidden ranking deals: users choose what to connect, data from connected apps is not used for model training, and Claude is meant to confirm before purchases or bookings. The broader play is obvious even if Anthropic doesn’t overstate it: Claude wants to become a single conversational layer across both work tools and personal services.

**Claude** 这次加的不只是工作软件，而是直接往日常生活里伸，接上了 **AllTrails**、**Instacart**、**Audible**、**Tripadvisor**、**TurboTax**、**Uber** 这些更偏消费场景的服务。Anthropic 还改了连接器的出现方式，不再让用户自己翻工具目录，而是根据上下文在对话里直接冒出来，比如订餐、买菜、查行程这种事，Claude 会自己提议该连哪个应用。

它强调的一点也挺直白：不做广告位，不搞付费排序，用户自己决定连什么，连接过来的数据也不拿去训练模型，真到下单或预订前还会先确认。说白了，Claude 想吃下的不只是办公入口，而是整层对话式操作界面。

sections.headline: **Cognition** ships long-horizon real-world evals for **Devin** / **Cognition** 放出面向 **Devin** 的长时程真实世界评测
sections.body:
Finally! the first eval ship from cog!!!!!!!!!! 👼🏼

To contextualize: @METR_Evals cap out at ~16 hours. 

Cog has private enterprise evals up to 100hrs, and is confident enough to put a financial guarantee on it 🤯

METR dataset: ML eng, GPU kernels, cybersecurity

> "METR (2026) used a combination of GPT-4o and GPT-5 to estimate the human-equivalent times from compressed Claude Code transcripts. These transcripts were collected from 7 METR technical staff on 34 sessions labeled on human ground truth". rlog​ of 0.83

Cog dataset: real life java/typescript/python/c# feature dev, bugfixes, migrations

> "We collected a ground-truth dataset by asking Devin users to review recent representative sessions, and estimate how long each completed session would have taken without Devin. Our dataset consists of 258 sessions from 126 users across a diverse set of enterprise customers." rlog​ of 0.74 on held out set

this is pioneering real world evals work and part 1 of a broader frontier code evals drop that I'm really looking forward to writing up. huge kudos to @annarmitchell and @ryanbai1412 for leading the unglamorous last mile data collection!!

终于！cog 发了第一份 eval!!!!!!!!!! 👼🏼

补个背景：@METR_Evals 现在大概到 ~16 小时封顶。

Cog 这边已经有面向企业私有场景、最长到 100 小时的评测，而且甚至敢给金融担保 🤯

METR 数据集：机器学习工程、GPU kernel、网络安全

> “METR（2026）使用 GPT-4o 和 GPT-5 的组合，从压缩后的 Claude Code 转录中估算等效人类耗时。这些转录来自 7 位 METR 技术成员的 34 次会话，并且有人类真实标注。” rlog 为 0.83

Cog 数据集：真实世界里的 java/typescript/python/c# 功能开发、修 bug、迁移

> “我们通过让 Devin 用户回看近期具有代表性的会话，并估算如果没有 Devin，这些已完成会话要花多久，来收集真实标注数据。数据集包含 126 位用户、来自多家企业客户的 258 次会话。” 留出集上的 rlog 为 0.74

这是真正在做真实世界评测的开路工作，也是更大一波前沿代码评测发布的第一部分。我很期待后面把它写出来。也得大力夸一下 @annarmitchell 和 @ryanbai1412，把这堆不光鲜但最难的最后一公里数据收集扛下来了！！

sections.headline: **Codex** wins on capability but loses on first-impression frontend / **Codex** 能力强，但前端第一眼观感还差点意思
sections.body:
Also as great as Codex is (and I'm really starting to love it) the frontend design still leaves alot to be desired. 

I have a /slides skill and you can guess which one Codex made vs. Claude.

Yes I know I can make an image with ChatGPT first and then tell Codex to build it but Claude can one shot great looking HTML slides.

Codex needs to fix this imo it's often a novice's first impression of a coding or knowledge work tool.

另外，Codex 虽然确实很强（而且我也越来越喜欢它了），但前端设计还是挺不够看的。

我有个 /slides skill，你基本一眼就能猜出哪个是 Codex 做的，哪个是 Claude 做的。

对，我知道我可以先用 ChatGPT 生成一张图，再让 Codex 去照着搭，但 Claude 现在就是能一把出很好看的 HTML 幻灯片。

我觉得 Codex 得把这件事补上，因为这往往就是新手对一个编程或知识工作工具的第一印象。

sections.headline: Set up **Codex** workflows first, save half your time later / 先把 **Codex** 工作流搭好，后面至少能省一半时间
sections.body:
I spent the whole day today setting up integrations and skills in Codex for my top creator workflows.

Now I'm convinced that you can save at least 50% of your time on any type of knowledge work if you just set up the system upfront.

Note that all my workflows have human checkpoints along the way so I can apply my "taste."

Anyway, it feels extremely liberating to have all this set up. If you want to do the same, just follow these three steps:

1. Reflect on your past week:
- What work did you spend the most time on?
- What work was the most repetitive?

Pick your most painful, manual workflow to start.

2. List out every single step of that manual workflow. Be very detail oriented.

3. Open Codex (or Claude Code) and paste the list of steps from 2 and ask it "What integrations and skills can I build to streamline this with your help?"

AI will guide you the rest of the way.

我今天一整天都在给自己最常用的创作者工作流配置 Codex 的 integrations 和 skills。

现在我基本确信，只要前面把系统搭好，任何知识工作都至少能省下 50% 的时间。

先说明一下：我的所有工作流里都会保留人工检查点，这样我还能把自己的“品味”放进去。

总之，全都搭好之后，整个人轻松很多。如果你也想这么做，就按这三步来：

1. 回看你过去一周：
- 什么工作最花时间？
- 什么工作最重复？

先挑那个最痛、最手工的流程下手。

2. 把这个手工流程的每一步全部列出来。越细越好。

3. 打开 Codex（或者 Claude Code），把第 2 步那份步骤清单贴进去，问它：“为了在你的帮助下把这件事变顺，我可以做哪些 integrations 和 skills？”

后面的路，AI 会继续带你走。

sections.headline: **Claude** now writes most of **Anthropic**’s code / **Claude** 现在已经写了 **Anthropic** 大部分代码
sections.body:
We just published internal data on how much of Claude's development is already being done by Claude:
- Over 80% of all code merged into our codebase is now written by Claude
- It's been months since many researchers at Anthropic hand-wrote code
- The typical Anthropic engineer ships 8x as much code as they did in 2024
- On the most open-ended engineering tasks, Claude's success rate jumped from ~26% to 76% in 6 months
- When research sessions went off-track, Claude proposed a better next step than the human took 64% of the time

We're not at recursive self-improvement yet, but it could come sooner than most expect. I highly recommend reading the full blog post.

我们刚发布了一组内部数据，讲 Claude 的开发工作里到底有多少已经是 Claude 自己在做：
- 现在合并进我们代码库的代码里，超过 80% 是 Claude 写的
- Anthropic 里很多研究员已经好几个月没亲手写代码了
- 一个典型的 Anthropic 工程师，现在交付的代码量是 2024 年的 8 倍
- 在最开放式的工程任务上，Claude 的成功率 6 个月内从大约 26% 跳到 76%
- 当研究会话跑偏时，Claude 提出的下一步有 64% 的时候比人类实际采取的那一步更好

我们还没到递归式自我改进那一步，但它也许会比多数人想得更早到来。我很推荐去看完整博客。

sections.headline: AI creates more ideas than organizations can execute / AI 带来的点子已经多到组织执行不过来
sections.body:
Good thought provoking post from Anthropic. I think this paragraph points to the key element of the optimistic scenario of AI:

“There has been an explosion of new ideas, initiatives, tools, and simulations, as a result of Anthropic employees working with highly capable models—far more than we have the capacity to pursue. The rate at which organizations can spot and fix these bottlenecks may be a skill that improves over time, and it may become the most important skill for any organization.”

AI lowers the barrier dramatically to allowing us to do more. As a result of that, we have far more ideas than we can pursue, and for the ones that we want to pursue we’re ultimately limited by our ability to go take on the surrounding work to execute those ideas. There’s almost no amount of AI progress that can happen where that goes away.

AI is going to let us build much more software, launch more marketing campaigns, research more drugs, and so on. All of this work, even when augmented by agents, still ultimately requires people to manage.

Anthropic 这篇挺值得想。我觉得下面这段抓住了 AI 乐观叙事里最关键的一点：

“随着 Anthropic 员工和高能力模型一起工作，新的点子、项目、工具和模拟出现了爆发式增长，已经远远超过我们的实际承接能力。一个组织能多快发现并修掉这些瓶颈，可能会成为会持续进化的能力，也可能会变成任何组织最重要的能力。”

AI 大幅降低了做更多事的门槛。结果就是，我们手里的想法会比能真正推进的多得多；而那些真想推进的事，最后还是受限于我们有没有能力把周边执行工作一起扛起来。这件事几乎不会因为 AI 再进步多少就自动消失。

AI 会让我们能写更多软件、发更多营销活动、研究更多药物，等等。哪怕这些工作都有 agent 帮忙，最终还是得有人去管。

sections.headline: Built a founder-eval skill from real investor meeting notes / 用真实投资会谈笔记做了一个看 deck 的技能
sections.body:
Introducing the Nock skill (powered by @meetgranola) 👀

Someone recently asked me if I can be replaced by AI, and my ego initially said NO WAY.. 

Then, I thought about what's the best way to have the most accurate "AI" representation of me for these conversations.

So, I used @claudeai Code to pull >200 1:1 founder pitch meeting notes that were captured by Granola in the last couple of years. 

Focused all the notes to only things I asked. Distilled it further down to ~53 meetings where there was a lot of good discussion and debate.

Finally, I took a few of my essays which describe the kind of founders that I love.

Using those, I used Claude Code again to build this skill called "Nock" that has some principles and a question bank that are grounded in real conversations. 

To refine, I used this skill over 5-10 actual decks and conversations where we first had the skill output what it thinks and then we compared it against the real conversation. We kept improving it - till it felt like an accurate representation of me. 

So, if you are a founder raising and want to see what I would think about your deck, try this out: nikunjk dot com / nock

And, if you are a VC who wants to build your own Nock, we have that too: nikunjk dot com / buildnock

介绍一下 Nock skill（由 @meetgranola 驱动）👀

最近有人问我，我会不会被 AI 取代，我的自尊第一反应当然是：不可能..

但后来我开始想，怎样才能做出一个在这类对话里最接近“我本人”的 AI 版本。

于是，我用 @claudeai Code 拉了过去几年里由 Granola 记录下来的 200 多份和创始人一对一 pitch 的会议笔记。

先只保留我提过的问题，再进一步压缩到大约 53 场讨论特别充分、来回交锋比较多的会议。

最后，我又加了几篇自己写的文章，里面讲的是我偏爱的创始人类型。

拿这些材料，我又用 Claude Code 做了一个叫 “Nock” 的 skill，里面有一些原则和一套问题库，底子都来自真实对话。

为了继续打磨，我拿这个 skill 跑了 5 到 10 个真实 deck 和真实对话，先让它输出自己的判断，再拿去和真实会谈对照。我们就这样一轮轮改，直到它开始像是一个靠谱的“我”。

如果你正在融资，想看看我会怎么想你的 deck，可以试试：nikunjk dot com / nock

如果你是 VC，也想做一个自己的 Nock，我们也有：nikunjk dot com / buildnock
